question:
(a) Using $R = R_{0}A^{1/3}$, show that the nuclear volume is proportional to mass number $A$.
(b) Explain how the short-range and saturation properties of nuclear force support the nearly constant density of nuclei.

options.A:
(a) From $R=R_0A^{1/3}$, $V\propto R\propto A^{1/3}$.
(b) This proves every nucleon strongly interacts with every other nucleon.
options.B:
(a) $V=\frac43\pi R^3=\frac43\pi(R_0A^{1/3})^3=\frac43\pi R_0^3A$, hence $V\propto A$.
(b) Nuclear force is short-ranged, so each nucleon interacts mainly with nearby neighbours (saturation). Thus mass and volume both grow roughly with $A$, giving nearly constant density.
options.C:
(a) $V\propto A^3$.
(b) Saturation means nuclear force becomes stronger over unlimited distances.
options.D:
(a) Nuclear volume is independent of $A$.
(b) Nuclear density is zero because nucleons do not interact.
